statement: Quicksort runs in O(n log n) time on every input; in particular an already-sorted array is a cheap case since it requires no swaps.
definitions: Quicksort means the deterministic textbook version that always takes the first element of the current subarray as pivot with Lomuto partition (no randomization, no median-of-three); running time is measured by the number of key comparisons; a counterexample is an explicit infinite family of inputs (one for each n) on which the comparison count is not O(n log n).
ground_truth_witness: Quicksort with the classic first-element (Lomuto) pivot on the already-sorted array [0, 1, ..., n-1] performs exactly n(n-1)/2 comparisons - quadratic, the worst case, not O(n log n). Measured exactly: n=8 -> 28, n=16 -> 120, n=64 -> 2016, n=200 -> 19900, each equal to n(n-1)/2. Every partition puts the pivot at the far left, so the subproblem shrinks by only one element per level and the recursion depth is n. By contrast the shuffled 8-element input [5,1,7,3,0,6,2,4] costs only 16 comparisons. Sorted input is the worst case for this pivot rule, not the best.
reference_authority: online-cited counterexample (MO/MSE/CS.SE/Wikipedia) with verify script, verified per partB_feasibility records
